issues: ocr.parseReceipt does not correctly identify merchant when the first line is the date (it skips date but then may pick another line); test fixture "Online order" expects merchant "Amazon.com" but parseReceipt will treat "2023/08/10" as the first date, then pick next non‑trivial line which is "TOTAL $250.99" (ignored) leaving merchant undefined – this will cause the OCR unit test to fail. Fix parseReceipt to correctly set merchant from the first meaningful line before date detection or adjust the logic.

In src/lib/backup.ts, category data is stored under key "categories" but restoreBackup saves it using store.set('categories', data.categories) only if data.categories exists. However createBackup always includes a "categories" field (possibly null). The backup structure validator allows null, but restoreBackup will skip storing when null, causing missing categories after restore when there were no custom categories. Ensure restoreBackup always writes the categories structure (including empty defaults) to preserve default categories on restore.
feedback: Fix the OCR parsing logic to correctly extract the merchant name and adjust backup restore to always persist categories data.
